svg.text: Each run owns its harness home, and a plan write has one route out
The fence seals the operator’s dot directories, so both writes a fenced worker must make are given a home inside its run.
A — what the run owns (sealed as a config home, and granted)
~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/
manifest.md
the run directory: rw
harness/
← CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
codex-home/
← CODEX_HOME
auth.json
--ro-bind of ~/.codex/auth.json
transcripts, sessions, rollouts and config land here, not in the
operator’s home. The home is seeded with the directory alone;
the login is bound, never copied, so a worker cannot shadow the
login the operator refreshes.
B — the MCP server a fenced worker starts is a child of the fence
edit_plan
reckon’s MCP server, spawned inside the fenced process
no checkout_path
refused: main checkout is sealed
checkout_path = worktree
lands in the worker’s worktree
both routes take a lock under ~/.config/reckon/locks/
a sealed lock directory refuses the worktree route too, so that
subtree is granted writable while the rest stays read-only
The refusal above is the target path, not the lock: the lock is taken, then the
write into the sealed main checkout fails with “Read-only file system” and the
file is byte-identical afterwards.
main file byte-identical · worktree file carries the edit
C — the declared negative control
leave CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset so the fenced stub writes under the stand-in ~/.claude
applied: the harness state write is refused under “Read-only file system” instead of landing in <run>/harness/,
and the stand-in ~/.claude holds only its sentinel. The plan-write measure is unmoved.
Both promises fail in the same direction: a home that is not the operator’s is the precondition for the fence being on.
Measured through launch_plan: the environment and the composed argv are asserted, then the argv is executed with a stub in place of the harness.
